mutants.description: The S_RUN count is updated as 'increment on a faulted entering sample, else decrement on a faulted leaving sample', forgetting the case where a faulted sample enters while a faulted one leaves, so it increments instead of holding.
mutants.reason: Once the 16-cycle run window has filled, any faulted cycle that coincides with a faulted cycle leaving the window raises the count. For example, with an overcurrent on every other cycle in S_RUN the true count is 8, but fault_count_run_out keeps climbing and window_trip asserts at trip_run even though it should not.

mutants.description: The soft-start count tests the leaving bit before the entering bit, so a cycle where a faulted sample leaves and a faulted sample enters decrements the count instead of holding it.
mutants.reason: With a periodic overcurrent in S_SS whose period divides 32 (every other cycle, say), fault_count_ss_out falls after the window fills, wraps below zero to a large value, and falsely asserts window_trip_SS.

mutants.description: The S_RUN count subtracts the most recent stored sample (bit 0, per the 'most recent cycle in bit 0' convention) instead of the oldest sample leaving the window at bit WINDOW_RUN-1.
mutants.reason: The count telescopes to just the latest sample (0 or 1), so in S_RUN fault_count_run_out never goes above 1. A sustained overcurrent never trips window_trip for any trip_run of 2 or more.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window and its count both take the blanked sample from the comparator BLANK_CLKS-1 clocks before high-side turn-on instead of BLANK_CLKS clocks before, so the run lookback is one clock short while soft start keeps the full lookback.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, a comparator pulse that is high exactly 4 clocks before pwm_rise but low 5 clocks before (or the reverse) is counted wrongly. fault_count_run_out and the timing of window_trip then differ from the correctly blanked sample.

mutants.description: Blanking is applied only to the S_RUN window: the soft-start window and its count both take the live cp_sync at pwm_rise instead of the blanked cp_delay sample.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, a comparator glitch present at the turn-on clock but absent BLANK_CLKS clocks earlier is counted as a faulted cycle, and a fault that ended inside the blanking interval is missed. This changes fault_count_ss_out and can falsely assert (or fail to assert) window_trip_SS.

mutants.description: The S_RUN trip counts one faulted cycle too many when comparing with trip_run, so window_trip asserts when the window holds trip_run-1 faulted cycles.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with exactly trip_run-1 faulted cycles in the window (11 with the default 12), window_trip asserts and the supervisor goes into hiccup. The correct design would keep running.

mutants.description: window_trip_SS is suppressed only in S_RUN instead of being allowed only in S_SS, so it is not gated in the idle and hiccup states.
mutants.reason: After a soft-start trip the supervisor leaves S_SS. On the first idle clock, before the idle clear empties the window, the count is still at or above trip_ss, so window_trip_SS stays high for an extra clock outside S_SS. The same happens throughout idle if trip_ss is 0.
